turns.assessment: The outage pattern is a digital OTN-layer failure centered on S15: every affected service uses S15, unprotected services are down, and SNCP services report protection unavailable, consistent with loss of their working ODU paths. Six simultaneous OTU framing alarms occurred while receiver power, OSNR, BER, DGD, amplifier telemetry, and channel monitors showed no optical change, strongly excluding a fibre, amplifier, connector, or WSS signal-loss event. A common OTN switch-fabric failure at S15 best explains the multi-service interruption without an optical disturbance.

proposals.rationale: All affected working paths depend on S15, with unprotected services down and protected services degraded after losing working-path availability. The simultaneous multi-channel framing failures with unchanged optical telemetry point to common digital switching equipment rather than the optical plant.
proposals.note: site named; resolved to its node equipment

proposals.rationale: A failed transmitting line card can cause OTU_LOF with otherwise normal upstream optical plant readings, but one card does not naturally explain six simultaneous lightpath alarms and the broad service pattern.

A failed WSS input port could affect multiple channels at S15, but it should produce optical signal loss or power changes downstream; the relevant receiver and channel-power instruments remained unchanged.
